title: Tracking the 2024 US Presidential Election Chatter on Tiktok: A Public Multimodal Dataset
extended_summary:
The provided paper is not the requested study titled “Impact of ChatGPT on the Academic Writing Quality of Senior High School Students” (2024). Instead, it is a working paper describing the construction and release of a large-scale public multimodal dataset of TikTok posts related to the 2024 U.S. presidential election. The paper’s central question is how to systematically collect and share election-related TikTok content so researchers can analyze political discourse, candidate-related chatter, and evolving communication patterns on the platform.

The authors’ approach is a large-scale observational data collection effort rather than an educational intervention study. They use the TikTok Research API to gather metadata for U.S.-published videos matching evolving election-related keywords and hashtags across five collection phases from November 1, 2023 to May 26, 2024, and supplement this with plans for third-party scraping to address API gaps. The released dataset includes nearly 1.8 million videos and associated metadata such as captions, hashtags, counts of views/likes/comments/shares, and a subset of TikTok-generated transcripts; the authors also discuss plans to generate additional transcripts using Whisper.

No educational participants, schools, teachers, or students are studied. The context is online social media discourse in the United States, specifically TikTok users posting election-related content. Analyses are descriptive and exploratory, focusing on common keywords, hashtags, language detection, and frequent bigrams in English and Spanish transcripts.

The paper concludes that TikTok contains substantial election-related discourse, especially around Joe Biden and Donald Trump, and that a public dataset can support future computational social science research. It also emphasizes important methodological limitations of the TikTok Research API, including rate limits, token expiration, incomplete transcript coverage, and temporal gaps in collected content, motivating the use of supplemental scrapers and future multimodal analyses.
quality_tier_rationale: The provided document is not the requested education study. It is a working paper describing a TikTok election dataset, with no K-12 educational intervention, no academic-writing sample, and no evaluative study design relevant to ChatGPT use in schools.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational impact evidence is reported because the supplied paper does not study student learning, writing quality, or any school-based intervention.
